syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Why study geography and what geography is

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin and meaning of the term geography and who coined it.
Distinguish physical features of the earth's surface from cultural features created by human beings.

topics.title: Areal differentiation, causal relationships and nature-human interaction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain geography as the study of areal differentiation and of the causes behind spatial variation.
Explain how human beings adapt to and modify nature, producing humanised nature and naturalised humans.

topics.title: The three questions of geography and spatial organisation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the what, where and why questions and explain why the why question made geography scientific.
Explain how links (routes) and nodes (settlements) organise and integrate space.
Explain geography as a discipline of spatial synthesis compared with history's temporal synthesis.
Analyse how geographical factors such as distance, mountains and seas have shaped historical events.
Explain how time and space can be converted into each other and why time is the fourth dimension.

topics.title: Branches of geography: approaches and sub-fields

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish the systematic approach of Humboldt from the regional approach of Ritter.
Classify sub-fields such as geomorphology, climatology, hydrology and political geography into physical, human and biogeography.
Identify the branches based on the regional approach and the philosophy and methods common to all branches.
Identify the four realms studied in physical geography and what each includes.
Evaluate the importance of physical geography for resource management and sustainable development.

chapters.title: The Origin and Evolution of the Earth

topics.title: Early Theories: Origin of the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the nebular hypothesis of Kant and Laplace and its revision by Otto Schmidt and Carl Weizascar.

topics.title: Origin of the Universe: the Big Bang Theory

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the stages in the development of the universe according to the Big Bang Theory.
Interpret the evidence for an expanding universe and contrast it with the steady state concept.
Explain how density differences in the early universe led to nebulae, galaxies and stars.
Use the light year as a measure of distance in simple calculations.
Sequence the stages by which planetesimals accreted into planets.

topics.title: Evolution of the Earth and its Lithosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Evolution of the Earth; Evolution of Lithosphere

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the layered structure of the earth and the change in density from crust to core.
Explain how differentiation separated earth material into layers.
Identify the three stages in the evolution of the present atmosphere.
Explain degassing and the formation of oceans and atmospheric oxygen.
Explain the origin of life as a chemical process and the fossil evidence for its age.

topics.title: Sources of information about the interior
topics.ncert_sections: Sources of information about the interior: direct and indirect sources

concepts.learning_objective: Identify mining, deep drilling and volcanic eruptions as direct sources of information about the earth's interior.
Explain how temperature, pressure, density, meteors, gravitation and magnetism give indirect evidence of the interior.
Interpret gravity anomalies as evidence of the distribution of mass in the crust.

topics.title: Earthquakes and earthquake waves
topics.ncert_sections: Earthquake; Why does the earth shake?; Earthquake waves; Propagation of earthquake waves

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how energy released along a fault produces an earthquake and define focus and epicentre.
Distinguish P-waves, S-waves and surface waves by speed, medium and destructiveness.
Explain how P-waves and S-waves vibrate relative to the direction of propagation.
Locate the shadow zones of P-waves and S-waves in terms of angular distance from the epicentre.
Infer the liquid nature of the outer core from the absence of S-waves beyond 105 degrees.

topics.title: Types, measurement and effects of earthquakes
topics.ncert_sections: Types of earthquakes; Measuring earthquakes; Effects of earthquake; Frequency of earthquake occurrences

concepts.learning_objective: Classify earthquakes as tectonic, volcanic, collapse, explosion and reservoir induced.
Distinguish the Richter magnitude scale from the Mercalli intensity scale.
Identify the hazardous effects of earthquakes and the conditions for a tsunami.

topics.title: Structure of the earth
topics.ncert_sections: Structure of the earth: the crust, the mantle, the core

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the thickness and nature of the oceanic and continental crust.
Describe the extent of the mantle, the asthenosphere and the lithosphere.
Describe the state and composition of the outer and inner core.

topics.title: Volcanoes
topics.ncert_sections: Volcanoes and volcanic landforms; Volcanoes (shield, composite, caldera, flood basalt, mid-ocean ridge)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish magma from lava and name the materials a volcano releases.
Compare shield, composite, caldera, flood basalt and mid-ocean ridge volcanoes.

topics.title: Intrusive volcanic landforms
topics.ncert_sections: Volcanic landforms: intrusive forms (batholiths, lacoliths, lapolith, phacolith, sills, dykes)

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish volcanic rocks from plutonic rocks by where the lava cools.
Identify batholiths, lacoliths, lapoliths, phacoliths, sills, sheets and dykes from their shape and position.

topics.title: Continental drift theory and its driving forces

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Wegener's continental drift theory, Pangaea, Panthalassa and the split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Explain the pole-fleeing and tidal forces proposed by Wegener and why they were rejected.

topics.title: Evidence in support of continental drift
topics.ncert_sections: Evidence in Support of the Continental Drift

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the jig-saw fit of coastlines and rocks of the same age across oceans support drift.
Interpret tillite, placer deposits and fossil distribution as evidence of continental drift.

topics.title: Post-drift studies and the ocean floor
topics.ncert_sections: Post-drift Studies; Convectional Current Theory; Mapping of the Ocean Floor; Ocean Floor Configuration; Distribution of Earthquakes and Volcanoes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain Arthur Holmes's convection current theory and its role in answering the problem of force.
Identify the divisions of the ocean floor: continental margins, abyssal plains and mid-oceanic ridges.
Interpret the global distribution of earthquakes and volcanoes and their focal depths.
Recall the facts about ocean-floor rocks, sediments and magnetism revealed by post-drift studies.
Explain Hess's hypothesis of sea floor spreading and the consumption of crust at trenches.

topics.title: Plate tectonics and plate boundaries
topics.ncert_sections: Plate Tectonics; Divergent, Convergent and Transform Boundaries

concepts.learning_objective: Define a tectonic plate and identify the major and minor plates of the world.
Distinguish divergent, convergent and transform plate boundaries with examples.

topics.title: Rate of plate movement and its driving force
topics.ncert_sections: Rates of Plate Movement; Force for the Plate Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how magnetic stripes give the rates of plate movement and compare slow and fast ridges.
Explain convection cells in the mantle as the force behind plate movement.
Identify the northern, eastern, western and southern boundaries of the Indian plate.
Describe India's northward journey, the Deccan Traps and the formation of the Himalayas.
Distinguish land-building endogenic forces from land-wearing exogenic forces and explain why relief persists.
Define a geomorphic agent and distinguish it from a geomorphic process.
Explain why gravity and gradients are essential for all surface movement of earth materials.
Identify the sources of energy that drive endogenic processes.
Describe orogenic, epeirogenic, earthquake and plate tectonic processes under diastrophism.
Explain what volcanism includes as an endogenic process.
Explain how solar energy, gravity and stresses drive exogenic processes.
State the processes included under denudation.
Analyse how climate and rock type and structure control rates of exogenic processes.

topics.title: Weathering
topics.ncert_sections: Weathering; Chemical, Physical and Biological Weathering; Special Effects; Significance

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish chemical, physical and biological weathering processes.
Explain exfoliation as a result of unloading and thermal expansion.
Evaluate the role of weathering in soils, erosion, biodiversity and ore enrichment.
Explain why mass movements are gravity-driven and not a form of erosion.
Identify the activating causes and favourable conditions for mass movements.
Distinguish slump, debris slide, debris fall, rockslide and rock fall.
Explain erosion and compare climatically and non-climatically controlled agents.
Explain deposition as a consequence of loss of energy of erosional agents.

topics.title: Soil formation
topics.ncert_sections: Soil Formation; Process of Soil Formation; Soil-forming Factors

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the stages of soil formation from the weathering mantle to mature soil.
Explain the role of parent material, topography and time as passive soil-forming factors.
Explain how climate and biological activity act as active soil-forming factors.

topics.title: Running water and stages of landscape evolution

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a landform from a landscape and explain what evolution of landforms means.
Describe the characteristics of youth, mature and old stages of landscapes shaped by running water.
Explain how stream erosion reduces relief to a peneplain with monadnocks.

topics.title: Erosional landforms of running water
topics.ncert_sections: Erosional Landforms: Valleys, Potholes and Plunge Pools, Incised Meanders, River Terraces

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between V-shaped valleys, gorges and canyons and relate them to rock type.
Explain the formation of potholes and plunge pools.
Explain incised meanders and river terraces as products of vertical erosion.

topics.title: Depositional landforms of running water
topics.ncert_sections: Depositional Landforms: Alluvial Fans, Deltas, Floodplains, Natural Levees, Point Bars, Meanders

concepts.learning_objective: Compare alluvial fans and deltas in location and sorting of deposits.
Distinguish floodplains, natural levees and point bars.
Explain why meanders develop and how ox-bow lakes form.
Explain why groundwater forms landforms mainly in limestone through solution and precipitation.
Describe swallow holes, sinkholes, uvalas, lapies and caves.
Explain the formation of stalactites, stalagmites and pillars.
Describe cirques, horns, aretes and glacial troughs formed by glacial erosion.
Distinguish till from outwash deposits and identify types of moraines.
Explain the formation of eskers, outwash plains and drumlins.

topics.title: Waves and currents: coastal landforms
topics.ncert_sections: Waves and Currents: High Rocky Coasts, Low Sedimentary Coasts, Erosional and Depositional Landforms

concepts.learning_objective: Compare high rocky coasts and low sedimentary coasts in processes and landforms.
Explain the formation of sea cliffs, wave-cut terraces, sea caves and stacks.
Explain how beaches, bars, barriers, spits and lagoons develop.
Explain deflation, abrasion and impact and the role of sheet floods in deserts.
Describe pediments, pediplains, playas, deflation hollows and mushroom rocks.
Distinguish barchans, parabolic, seif, longitudinal and transverse dunes.

topics.title: Atmosphere and its gases
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Composition of the Atmosphere; Gases

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the atmosphere as a mixture of gases enveloping the earth and state where most of its mass lies.
Explain why carbon dioxide is meteorologically important and how its rising volume affects air temperature.
Explain the role of ozone in absorbing ultra-violet rays.
Explain how water vapour varies with altitude and latitude and how it regulates the earth's temperature.
Identify sources and distribution of dust particles and their role as hygroscopic nuclei.

topics.title: Troposphere and tropopause
topics.ncert_sections: Structure of the Atmosphere: troposphere, tropopause

concepts.learning_objective: State the five layers of the atmosphere and the basis of the division.
Explain the thickness, rate of temperature decrease and importance of the troposphere.
Describe the temperature conditions at the tropopause.

topics.title: Upper layers of the atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Structure of the Atmosphere: stratosphere, mesosphere, ionosphere, exosphere

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the extent of the stratosphere and the importance of its ozone layer.
Describe the temperature trend in the mesosphere and the features of the ionosphere.
Describe the nature of the exosphere.
Identify the main elements of weather and climate that influence human life.

chapters.title: Solar Radiation, Heat Balance and Temperature

concepts.learning_objective: Define insolation and state the average energy received at the top of the atmosphere.
Explain how the changing earth-sun distance at aphelion and perihelion affects insolation.

topics.title: Variability, passage and spatial distribution of insolation
topics.ncert_sections: Variability of Insolation; Passage of Solar Radiation; Spatial Distribution of Insolation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors that cause variation in the amount and intensity of insolation.
Describe what happens to solar radiation as it passes through the atmosphere.
Explain the pattern of insolation received at the earth's surface across latitudes.

topics.title: Heating and cooling of the atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: Heating and Cooling of Atmosphere; Terrestrial Radiation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how conduction heats the lower layers of the atmosphere.
Distinguish between vertical (convection) and horizontal (advection) transfer of heat.
Explain why the atmosphere is heated indirectly by long wave terrestrial radiation.

topics.title: Heat budget of the planet earth
topics.ncert_sections: Heat Budget of the Planet Earth; Variation in the Net Heat Budget

concepts.learning_objective: State the share of insolation reflected back to space as the earth's albedo.
Account for the units of energy absorbed and radiated in the earth's heat budget.
Explain the latitudinal surplus and deficit in net radiation and its redistribution.

topics.title: Temperature and factors controlling its distribution

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between heat and temperature.
Apply the normal lapse rate to estimate temperature change with altitude.
Explain how distance from the sea, air masses and ocean currents affect temperature.
Define isotherms and relate their general trend to latitude.
Compare the distribution of temperature in January and July in the two hemispheres.
Calculate and interpret the annual range of temperature.
Explain the conditions and effects of temperature inversion.
Explain air drainage and its effect in hills and valleys.

topics.title: Atmospheric Pressure and its Distribution
topics.ncert_sections: Atmospheric Pressure; Vertical Variation of Pressure; Horizontal Distribution of Pressure; World Distribution of Sea Level Pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how atmospheric pressure is measured and how it decreases with height.
Describe isobars and the world pattern of sea level pressure belts and their seasonal shift.

topics.title: Forces Affecting the Velocity and Direction of Wind
topics.ncert_sections: Forces Affecting the Velocity and Direction of Wind; Pressure Gradient Force; Frictional Force; Coriolis Force

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the pressure gradient force and friction influence wind speed.
Explain how the Coriolis force deflects winds and why it varies with latitude.
Describe the geostrophic wind as a balance of pressure gradient and Coriolis forces.
Distinguish cyclonic and anticyclonic circulation and the associated convergence and divergence.

topics.title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
topics.ncert_sections: General circulation of the atmosphere; General Atmospheric Circulation and its Effects on Oceans

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Hadley, Ferrel and polar cells and the planetary winds they produce.
Explain El Nino, the southern oscillation and the global effects of ENSO.

topics.title: Seasonal and Local Winds
topics.ncert_sections: Seasonal Wind; Local Winds; Land and Sea Breezes; Mountain and Valley Winds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the daily reversal of land and sea breezes from differential heating.
Explain valley breezes, mountain winds, katabatic winds and warm leeward winds.
Define an air mass and classify air masses by their source regions.
Identify the types of fronts and the weather they bring.
Describe the development and occlusion of an extra tropical cyclone along the polar front.
Compare extra tropical cyclones with tropical cyclones.
State the conditions for the formation of tropical cyclones and the source of their energy.
Describe the eye, eye wall and landfall of a mature tropical cyclone.
Explain how thunderstorms and tornadoes form.
Define absolute humidity and state its unit.
Explain relative humidity and how it changes with temperature.
Explain saturated air and the dew point.
Describe evaporation and the role of latent heat of vaporisation.
Explain how temperature, dryness and air movement affect evaporation.
Explain condensation, condensation nuclei and its causes.
Identify the conditions under which condensation takes place.

topics.title: Forms of condensation: dew, frost, fog and mist

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish dew and frost and the conditions for their formation.
Distinguish fog, mist and smog by visibility, moisture and location.
Identify cirrus, cumulus, stratus and nimbus clouds by height and appearance.
Classify combined cloud types into high, middle, low and vertical-development groups.
Explain how precipitation occurs and its liquid and solid forms.
Distinguish sleet and hailstones by their formation.
Explain the formation and distribution of convectional rain.
Explain orographic rain and the rain-shadow area.
Describe latitudinal, coastal and windward patterns of rainfall distribution.
Classify regions by annual precipitation regime.

topics.title: Approaches to classification and Koeppen's scheme
topics.ncert_sections: Koeppen's Scheme of Classification of Climate

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between empirical, genetic and applied approaches to classifying climate.
Explain how Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and letter codes to define climatic groups and types.
Describe the location and features of the Af, Am and Aw climate types.
Explain where and why dry climates occur at low and middle latitudes.
Compare subtropical steppe and desert climates.
Explain the location and the hot dry summer and rainy winter of the Mediterranean climate.
Describe the Cwa, Cfa and Cfb climate types and their locations.

topics.title: Cold snow forest and polar climates (Groups D and E)
topics.ncert_sections: Cold Snow Forest Climates (D); Polar Climates (E)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the distribution and features of the Df and Dw climate types.
Describe the tundra climate, permafrost and its vegetation.
Explain the features of the ice cap climate and how icebergs form.

topics.title: Climate change: evidence and the past
topics.ncert_sections: Climate Change; Climate in the recent past

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the geological, biological and historical evidence that climate changes naturally.
Recall major climatic episodes of the geological and recent past, including India.
Explain sunspots and Milankovitch oscillations as astronomical causes of climate change.
Explain how volcanic aerosols and human greenhouse gas emissions change climate.
Explain the greenhouse effect using the analogy of a glasshouse.
Identify the main greenhouse gases, their sources and sinks, and what makes a GHG effective.
Interpret the 20th-century temperature record, the impacts of warming and the Kyoto Protocol.
Describe the hydrological cycle and identify its components and processes.
State how the earth's water is distributed and explain why water crisis arises.

topics.title: Relief of the Ocean Floor: Major Divisions
topics.ncert_sections: Relief of the Ocean Floor; Divisions of the Ocean Floors

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the gradient, width, depth and significance of the continental shelf and slope.
Describe deep sea plains and oceanic deeps and their link with plate movements.

topics.title: Minor Relief Features of the Ocean Floor

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish mid-oceanic ridges, seamounts and guyots with examples.
Describe submarine canyons and atolls with examples.

topics.title: Factors Affecting Ocean Temperature
topics.ncert_sections: Temperature of Ocean Waters; Factors Affecting Temperature Distribution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how latitude, land-water distribution, winds and currents affect ocean temperature.

topics.title: Horizontal and Vertical Distribution of Temperature
topics.ncert_sections: Horizontal and Vertical Distribution of Temperature

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the three-layer thermal structure of oceans and the thermocline.
Interpret the variation of surface temperature with latitude and hemisphere.
Define salinity and state how it is expressed.
Explain the factors that influence the salinity of ocean water.

topics.title: Horizontal and Vertical Distribution of Salinity
topics.ncert_sections: Horizontal Distribution of Salinity; Vertical Distribution of Salinity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain regional variations in salinity of oceans and seas.
Describe the vertical variation of salinity, the halocline and stratification.

topics.title: Horizontal and vertical motions of ocean water

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between the horizontal (currents, waves) and vertical (tides, upwelling, sinking) motions of ocean water.
Explain how wind gives energy to waves and why waves slow down and break near the shore.
Define wave crest, trough, height, amplitude, period, wavelength, speed and frequency.
Explain how the moon's and sun's gravity and the centrifugal force produce two tidal bulges.
Explain how continental shelves, islands, bays and estuaries modify tides and how tides differ from surges.
Distinguish semi-diurnal, diurnal and mixed tides.
Explain spring and neap tides from the relative positions of the sun, moon and earth.
Relate perigee, apogee, perihelion and aphelion to tidal range, and define ebb and flow.
Explain the uses of tides in navigation, fishing, desilting and tidal power.

topics.title: Ocean currents and the forces behind them

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how solar heating, wind, gravity and the Coriolis force start and steer ocean currents.
Explain how differences in temperature and salinity drive the sinking and rising of water.

topics.title: Types and major ocean currents
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Ocean Currents; Major Ocean Currents; Characteristics of Ocean Currents

concepts.learning_objective: Classify ocean currents by depth and by temperature and state where warm and cold currents usually flow.
Relate ocean circulation to atmospheric circulation and describe the drift (speed) of currents.
Explain how warm and cold currents affect the climate of coastal regions.
Explain why the mixing of warm and cold currents creates rich fishing grounds.
Define biodiversity as the number and variety of organisms, their genes and ecosystems in a region.
Explain why biodiversity is uneven on the earth and richest in the tropics.
Describe genetic diversity as variation of genes within a species.
Explain species diversity and how it is measured.
Explain ecosystem diversity and why ecosystem boundaries are hard to demarcate.
Explain how species diversity makes ecosystems stable and productive.
Identify the economic commodities and agro-biodiversity that biodiversity supplies.
Explain the scientific and ethical value of every species.
Analyse the human and natural causes of biodiversity loss, including exotic species.
Distinguish between endangered, vulnerable and rare species as classified by IUCN.
Describe the Earth Summit, the world conservation strategy and India's Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
Explain mega diversity centres and biodiversity hotspots.
